new.title: Look up at Rouen's Gothic cathedral that Monet painted
new.desc: Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Rouen was begun in the 12th century and is the great Flamboyant Gothic church of Normandy, with a cast-iron spire of 151 m. It holds the tombs of Duke Rollo and Richard the Lionheart's heart. Monet painted its west facade about thirty times in 1892-1893.
new.tip: Free to enter; visit in the morning when the west front is in light. In summer a light show is projected on the facade at night.
new.q: Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Rouen, Place de la Cathédrale, Rouen

new.title: Climb the belfry of the Gros-Horloge astronomical clock
new.desc: The Gros-Horloge is a 14th-century astronomical clock set in a Renaissance arch spanning the rue du Gros-Horloge. The adjoining belfry holds bells dating in part from the 13th century and ends with a view over the city.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday with seasonal hours; the stairs are narrow, so it is not suited to reduced mobility. Check current hours at rouen.fr.
new.q: Gros-Horloge, Rue du Gros-Horloge, Rouen

new.title: Admire the Flamboyant facade of the Palais de Justice
new.desc: Begun in 1499 on the orders of Louis XII to house the Exchequer of Normandy, the palace is a late example of civil Flamboyant Gothic with Renaissance hints. It was heavily damaged in 1944 and restored; it still houses the court of appeal.
new.tip: Best seen from the courtyard on the rue aux Juifs side; the facade is lit at night. Interior access is limited to court hours.
new.q: Palais de Justice de Rouen, Rue Aux Juifs, Rouen

new.title: Hear the Cavaillé-Coll organ in Saint-Ouen abbey church
new.desc: The abbatiale Saint-Ouen is a Gothic abbey church whose grand organ was rebuilt by Aristide Cavaillé-Coll in 1890 inside a 1630 case. It is regarded as one of the most recorded organs in the world.
new.tip: Sunday afternoon organ concerts are held at 5 p.m. and the Festival des Orgues Cavaillé-Coll runs in August; check dates on the Rouen agenda.
new.q: Abbatiale Saint-Ouen, Place du Général de Gaulle, Rouen

new.title: Walk the timbered ossuary courtyard of the Aître Saint-Maclou
new.desc: This rare medieval charnel house was built from 1526 to 1533 around a cemetery used after the 1348 plague. It served as the fine arts school from 1940 to 2014 and has been restored as a cultural site.
new.tip: Free to enter the courtyard; look for the carved skulls and bones on the timber galleries and the mummified black cat.
new.q: Aître Saint-Maclou, 186 Rue Martainville, Rouen

new.title: See Renaissance glass in the Joan of Arc church
new.desc: Completed in 1979 by architect Louis Arretche on the site where Joan of Arc was burned in 1431, the church's roofline evokes flames. It reuses thirteen 16th-century stained-glass windows saved from the Saint-Vincent church destroyed in 1944.
new.tip: Free; combine with the covered market halls beside it and the Joan of Arc memorial cross on the square.
new.q: Église Sainte-Jeanne-d'Arc, Place du Vieux-Marché, Rouen

new.title: See Caravaggio and Monet at the Musée des Beaux-Arts
new.desc: The museum holds about 8,000 works from the 15th century on, including Caravaggio's Flagellation of Christ (c. 1607). The 1909 François Depeaux gift gives it one of the largest Impressionist collections in France outside Paris, with Monet and Sisley.
new.tip: Check the museum site for current opening times and admission; allow two hours for the main galleries.
new.q: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rouen, Esplanade Marcel Duchamp, Rouen

new.title: Browse wrought ironwork in the Le Secq des Tournelles museum
new.desc: The Musée Le Secq des Tournelles occupies the deconsecrated church of Saint-Laurent and displays the world's largest public collection of historic ironwork. It grew from a 1921 gift by collector Henri Le Secq des Tournelles.
new.tip: Admission to the Rouen metropolitan museums is free, according to local listings; confirm hours before going. Allow about an hour.
new.q: Musée Le Secq des Tournelles, 2 Rue Jacques Villon, Rouen

new.title: Discover Rouen faience at the Musée de la Céramique
new.desc: Housed in the 17th-century Hôtel d'Hocqueville, the museum shows Rouen faience from Masséot Abaquesne's 16th-century tiles to its 18th-century golden age, alongside Delft and Nevers wares. Its roots lie in the collection of historian André Pottier.
new.tip: Check opening days on the Rouen museums site; the rooms were fully reopened after a redisplay.
new.q: Musée de la Céramique, 1 Rue Faucon, Rouen

new.title: Enter the painted basilica of Notre-Dame de Bonsecours
new.desc: Designed by Jacques-Eugène Barthélemy, the neo-Gothic basilica was begun in 1840 and is described as the first example of the style in France. Its walls and vaults are fully painted, and it overlooks the Seine from the eastern edge of the city.
new.tip: Walk out to the Côte Sainte-Catherine belvedere afterwards for the panorama of Rouen and the Seine loops.
new.q: Basilique Notre-Dame de Bonsecours, Rue de la Basilique, Bonsecours

new.title: Visit Flaubert's riverside pavilion at Croisset
new.desc: The Pavillon Flaubert at 18 quai Gustave Flaubert in Dieppedalle-Croisset (Canteleu) is a survivor of the family house where Flaubert wrote Madame Bovary. It displays portraits, engravings, writing equipment and views of 19th-century Croisset.
new.tip: Free entry; opening hours are seasonal, so check with the Rouen museums network. Bus line 44 stops at the door.
new.q: Pavillon Flaubert, 18 Quai Gustave Flaubert, Canteleu

new.title: Relive Joan of Arc's trial at the Historial
new.desc: The Historial Jeanne d'Arc opened in 2015 in part of the former archbishop's palace, where sessions of her 1431 condemnation trial and her rehabilitation hearings took place. A multimedia route retraces her story and the archbishopric halls are included.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. per the 2024 guide (about 11 EUR); check historial-jeannedarc.fr.
new.q: Historial Jeanne d'Arc, 7 Rue Saint-Romain, Rouen

new.title: Study the five-porch facade of Église Saint-Maclou
new.desc: Built between about 1437 and 1517, Saint-Maclou is a jewel of Flamboyant Gothic, known for its five-porch west front and carved Renaissance wooden doors. It was damaged by bombing in 1944 and has been restored since.
new.tip: Free entry; the Portail des Fontaines on the left has the finest door carving. Pair with the adjoining Aître Saint-Maclou.
new.q: Église Saint-Maclou, Rue Martainville, Rouen

new.title: Climb the keep of Philippe Auguste's castle (Tour Jeanne d'Arc)
new.desc: The Tour Jeanne d'Arc is the last remnant of the castle Philippe Auguste built around 1210; the castle was dismantled from 1591. Joan of Arc was not held here but was threatened with torture in this keep during her 1431 trial.
new.tip: Guided and seasonal visits only; check the city website for hours before heading to the rue Bouvreuil.
new.q: Donjon de Rouen (Tour Jeanne d'Arc), Rue du Donjon, Rouen

new.title: Stroll the glasshouses of the Jardin des Plantes
new.desc: The 8-hectare Jardin des Plantes opened to the public in 1840 and mixes French and English garden styles. Its glasshouses, including tropical orchid houses and a palmarium, were renovated and reopened in 2019.
new.tip: Free, open from 8:30 a.m. to dusk; dogs and bikes are not allowed. The garden is on the left bank on avenue des Martyrs-de-la-Résistance.
new.q: Jardin des Plantes de Rouen, Avenue des Martyrs de la Résistance, Rouen

new.title: Wander the Cimetière Monumental, Rouen's Père-Lachaise
new.desc: Opened in 1828 on the northern slope of the city, the cemetery is often compared to Père-Lachaise. Among those buried are Pierre Corneille's family, poet Louis Bouilhet and Théodore Bachelet; it has been labelled a remarkable cemetery of Europe.
new.tip: Free; pick up the Métropole's visitor plan at the entrance and enter from the avenue Olivier de Serres side.
new.q: Cimetière Monumental de Rouen, Avenue Olivier de Serres, Rouen

new.title: Find the Field of the Cloth of Gold in the Bourgtheroulde courtyard
new.desc: The Hôtel de Bourgtheroulde is an early 16th-century mansion whose Italian-style Galerie d'Aumale carries a bas-relief of the 1520 meeting at the Field of the Cloth of Gold. Its facades are listed (1924) and it has been a luxury hotel since 2010.
new.tip: Ask at the hotel reception to see the courtyard gallery, or have a coffee in the hotel; visits depend on hotel access.
new.q: Hôtel de Bourgtheroulde, 15 Place de la Pucelle, Rouen

new.title: Visit Flaubert's birthplace and the history of medicine museum
new.desc: The Musée Flaubert et d'Histoire de la Médecine occupies the former Hôtel-Dieu pavilion where Flaubert was born and where his father worked as a surgeon. Founded in 1901, it shows pharmacy jars, medical instruments and Flaubert memorabilia.
new.tip: Free entry per the Rouen museums network; hours vary, so check before visiting. The small garden is a quiet stop.
new.q: Musée Flaubert et d'Histoire de la Médecine, 51 Rue Lecat, Rouen

new.title: Order canard à la rouennaise at La Couronne
new.desc: La Couronne on the Vieux-Marché claims to be France's oldest inn, dating from 1345. The house specialty is canard à la rouennaise, carved and pressed at the table with a silver duck press.
new.tip: Gault&Millau cites roughly 29 to 68 EUR per person excluding drinks; book ahead for weekends.
new.q: La Couronne, 31 Place du Vieux-Marché, Rouen

new.title: Buy Larmes de Jeanne d'Arc chocolates at Auzou
new.desc: Chocolaterie Auzou, on the rue du Gros-Horloge, makes the Larmes de Jeanne d'Arc, a nougatine almond-and-hazelnut sweet dipped in chocolate and rolled in cocoa.
new.tip: Sold in boxes of 120 g or more; the shop is a short step from the Gros-Horloge. Check current hours at the shop.
new.q: Chocolaterie Auzou, 163 Rue du Gros-Horloge, Rouen

new.title: Dine on the quay at Gill, Rouen's chef's table
new.desc: Chef Gilles Tournadre ran Gill as Rouen's only two-star restaurant for 36 years before asking to leave the Michelin system in 2020. It stays highly rated by Gault&Millau, on the quai de la Bourse by the Seine.
new.tip: Menus of about 49 and 89 EUR were quoted in 2024, with a la carte from 26 EUR; reservations are advisable.
new.q: Gill, 8-9 Quai de la Bourse, Rouen

new.title: Shop the Halles du Vieux-Marché and eat from the stalls
new.desc: The slate-and-copper market halls beside the Joan of Arc church are open Tuesday to Sunday with fruit, vegetable, flower and fish stalls. Fishmongers here supply nearby restaurants such as Le Comptoir des Halles.
new.tip: Go on a weekday morning for the freshest produce and fewer crowds.
new.q: Halles du Vieux-Marché, Place du Vieux-Marché, Rouen

new.title: Taste a pistachio éclair at Ma Boulangerie
new.desc: Christophe Cressent, a Meilleur Ouvrier de France, runs this bakery, which Gault&Millau calls the reference bakery of Rouen. Reviewers praise its baguettes, croissants, pistachio éclair and caramel tarts.
new.tip: Queues form around lunchtime; buy a baguette and a pastry for a picnic on the quays.
new.q: Ma Boulangerie, Rue Armand Carrel, Rouen

new.title: Queue for the traditional baguette at Maison Yvonne
new.desc: Maison Yvonne, at 119 rue Jeanne d'Arc, is known for choux, éclairs and bread; Gault&Millau notes people queue even in the rain for its traditional baguette. It also has other shops in the centre.
new.tip: Try the choux or an éclair with the baguette; weekday mornings are calmest.
new.q: Maison Yvonne, 119 Rue Jeanne d'Arc, Rouen

new.title: Eat a galette and Norman cider on the Robec at La Cornaelle
new.desc: La Cornaelle is a crêperie at 174 rue Eau-de-Robec with a terrace beside the little Robec stream among the timber-framed houses. Reviewers recommend pairing a savoury buckwheat galette with a local Norman cider.
new.tip: Sit on the terrace in good weather; phone 02 35 08 53 75 to check opening times.
new.q: La Cornaelle, 174 Rue Eau de Robec, Rouen

new.title: Drink Viking-style beer in the Ragnar church-brewery
new.desc: Brasserie Ragnar took over the deconsecrated Saint-Nicaise church after winning the city's call for projects in 2019. Its bar serves beers inspired by ancestral Viking recipes, mead and Normandy cider with local cheese and charcuterie.
new.tip: The beer garden opens in the warm season only; confirm opening hours before going.
new.q: Brasserie Ragnar, Église Saint-Nicaise, Rue Saint-Nicaise, Rouen

new.title: Take tea at Dame Cakes below the cathedral
new.desc: Dame Cakes is a tea room and pastry shop at 70 rue Saint-Romain in a building over a century old with a Louis XV-style interior. Its terrace looks toward the cathedral.
new.tip: Come for afternoon tea after the cathedral; the terrace is popular in fine weather.
new.q: Dame Cakes, 70 Rue Saint-Romain, Rouen

new.title: Eat a hearty Norman gratin at Le P'tit Bec
new.desc: Le P'tit Bec, at 182 rue Eau-de-Robec, serves Norman and traditional French dishes such as gratins, salads, confit de canard and homemade pastries. Frommer's lists main courses at roughly 14.50 to 19.50 EUR.
new.tip: A budget-friendly lunch stop in the Saint-Maclou quarter; check opening days on the tourist office listing.
new.q: Le P'tit Bec, 182 Rue Eau de Robec, Rouen

new.title: Try canard à la rouennaise at Les Capucines, Petit-Quevilly
new.desc: Run by the Demoget family for three generations, Les Capucines is described by Michelin as a Rouen institution of traditional cooking. Its listed specialty is duckling à la rouennaise and it has an extended list of lesser-known French wines.
new.tip: Mid-range prices (€€); book ahead, especially on weekends.
new.q: Les Capucines, Le Petit-Quevilly

new.title: Eat modern bistronomy at Paul-Arthur on Place de la Pucelle
new.desc: Paul-Arthur, at 23-25 place de la Pucelle, serves modern bistronomic cooking and holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand according to guide listings. It sits on one of the city's most photogenic squares.
new.tip: Reserve ahead for dinner; the set menu is the best value.
new.q: Paul-Arthur, 23-25 Place de la Pucelle, Rouen

new.title: Buy sucre de pomme made weekly at Les Confiseurs
new.desc: Les Confiseurs in Notre-Dame-de-Bondeville makes Rouen's traditional sucre de pomme, a hard candy often sold as a Rouen barley sugar, on site each week in four sizes. A cherry version also exists.
new.tip: Located at 12 rue de l'Abbaye; hours are not listed reliably, so check by phone or on lesconfiseurs.com first.
new.q: Les Confiseurs, 12 Rue de l'Abbaye, Notre-Dame-de-Bondeville

new.title: Climb the 525 steps to the Côte Sainte-Catherine belvedere
new.desc: A stepped path of roughly 525 steps climbs from the Martainville district to the belvedere on the Côte Sainte-Catherine, about 140 m up. The view takes in Rouen, its bridges and the Seine meanders.
new.tip: A development project for the site was under public enquiry in early 2026, so check access; you can also drive up the route de la Corniche.
new.q: Côte Sainte-Catherine, Route de la Corniche, Rouen

new.title: Hike the Forêt de Roumare from Canteleu
new.desc: The Forêt de Roumare north-west of Rouen has marked circuits from Canteleu, including a 7.5 km Circuit des 13 chênes and longer loops of around 21 km. Roe deer, red deer and wild boar live in the forest.
new.tip: Start from the parking by the Canteleu swimming pool; some waymarks are poorly maintained, so carry a GPS track.
new.q: Piscine de Canteleu, Canteleu

new.title: Take a cruise on the Seine meanders from the Rouen quays
new.desc: Boat trips leave from the quai Ferdinand de Lesseps. Bodega&Co Croisière offers an hour-and-a-half cruise along the Seine meanders, and L'Escapade is a restaurant boat with glazed lounges and panoramic terraces.
new.tip: Sailings are seasonal; book via the tourist office or the operator.
new.q: Quai Ferdinand de Lesseps, Rouen

new.title: Cycle La Seine à Vélo from Rouen to La Bouille
new.desc: The 19.56 km Rouen to La Bouille stage of La Seine à Vélo runs entirely on cycle paths and greenways. Take care on the busy Rouen quays, which have no barrier against falls into the river.
new.tip: Rent bikes at the tourist office on place de la Cathédrale or on the Esplanade Marcel Duchamp from May to September.
new.q: Esplanade Marcel Duchamp, Rouen

new.title: See the tall ships at the Armada de Rouen 2027
new.desc: The ninth Armada de Rouen is scheduled for 17 to 27 June 2027, bringing tall ships and historic vessels to the Seine quays with concerts and shows. It is held roughly every four to six years.
new.tip: Dates come from the organisers' announcement; expect crowds and book accommodation early.
new.q: Quais de Seine, Rive droite, Rouen

new.title: Join the Fêtes Jeanne d'Arc and Médiévales in May
new.desc: Rouen's Fêtes Jeanne d'Arc ran for their fifth edition on 14 to 16 May 2026, with a parade from the cathedral to the Vieux-Marché and the free Médiévales de Rouen, including craft demonstrations.
new.tip: Public transport has been free during the festival; it falls in mid-to-late May, so check the date each year.
new.q: Place du Vieux-Marché, Rouen

new.title: Watch the Cathédrale de Lumière show on the facade
new.desc: On summer evenings a son-et-lumière projection is cast onto the cathedral's west front; the 2026 edition adds a new tableau, Première floraison by Mika Ninagawa. The 2026 run listed goes to 26 September.
new.tip: It starts at nightfall; check the Métropole site for exact times and whether tickets are required.
new.q: Cathédrale Notre-Dame de Rouen, Place de la Cathédrale, Rouen

new.title: Browse the organic and flea stalls at Marché Saint-Marc
new.desc: The market under the halls on place Saint-Marc runs Friday to Sunday, focused on organic and local produce, with secondhand dealers' stalls that draw bargain hunters.
new.tip: Best on Saturday morning; hours for the flea stalls are about 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. Friday and Saturday and until 1:30 p.m. on Sunday per listings.
new.q: Place Saint-Marc, Rouen

new.title: Paddle a kayak on the Seine from Île Lacroix
new.desc: Kayak outings from the Espace Jacques Anquetil on Île Lacroix paddle the Seine meanders with views of the cathedral. Listings show a base rate from 20 EUR.
new.tip: Book in advance via the operator; clubs such as Pagaies en Seine at Belbeuf also run summer sunset paddles.
new.q: Espace Jacques Anquetil, Île Lacroix, Rouen

new.title: Follow the Normandie Impressionniste festival in Rouen
new.desc: The Festival Normandie Impressionniste ran 29 May to 27 September in 2026, with Rouen walks such as Rouen vue par Monet, Pissarro et Cie on selected Sundays, plus exhibitions and workshops.
new.tip: Dates shift each festival edition; the official site normandie-impressionniste.fr has the programme.
new.q: Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rouen, Esplanade Marcel Duchamp, Rouen

new.title: Stroll the rue Eau-de-Robec past timber-framed houses
new.desc: This semi-pedestrian street in the east of Rouen follows the little Robec stream, once the haunt of cloth makers and dyers. Timbered houses with drying lofts line it, and Flaubert called it the little Venice.
new.tip: Start at Église Saint-Maclou and walk along the stream; cafés and crêperies with terraces line the way.
new.q: Rue Eau de Robec, Rouen
